mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the federal funds rate over the prior month signals an accommodative monetary policy stance that reduces the cost of capital for corporations, leading to higher equity valuations and positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of instances where FEDFUNDS has declined over the prior month, or the Rank IC falls below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate exceeds 1.5% in the prior month, it signals a tightening monetary policy that increases borrowing costs and reduces corporate profitability, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of instances where FEDFUNDS > 1.5%, or the Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in the federal funds rate and a decline in the unemployment rate signals a tightening monetary policy coinciding with a strong labor market, which typically leads to higher inflation expectations and reduced equity valuations, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
regime_hint: tightening cycle with strong labor market
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of instances where FEDFUNDS rises and UNRATE falls, or the Rank IC for the interaction term falls below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate falls below 4.0%, it indicates a tight labor market that supports corporate profit growth and reduces recession risk, resulting in positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of instances where UNRATE < 4.0%, or the Rank IC for the UNRATE < 4.0% condition falls below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in non-farm payroll employment (PAYEMS) over the prior month indicates robust labor market conditions that support consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of instances where PAYEMS increases, or the Rank IC falls below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When housing starts (HOUST) fall below 1200.0 thousand units in the prior month, it signals a weakening in the residential construction sector, which is a key component of consumer spending, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of instances where HOUST < 1200.0, or the Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in housing starts (HOUST) and an increase in industrial production (INDPRO) signals a contraction in the residential sector coupled with a strengthening in manufacturing, which typically indicates a shift in economic activity that reduces equity valuations, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of instances where HOUST falls and INDPRO rises, or the Rank IC for the interaction term falls below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: In a regime of high industrial production growth (INDPRO > 105.0), the manufacturing sector's strength indicates robust economic activity that supports corporate earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of instances where INDPRO > 105.0, or the Rank IC for the INDPRO > 105.0 condition falls below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.
